findings.name: Kaal Sarp Dosha
findings.text: All seven classical planets are hemmed on one side of the Rahu-Ketu nodal axis. A popular modern astrological concept linked to non-linear progress and sudden turning points; should be judged in the context of the whole chart.

findings.name: Ascendant Lord in 5th House
findings.text: Sun, the ascendant lord, is in the 5th house: sharp intellect, creative inclinations and wise discernment; blessed with merits from past deeds and good progeny.

findings.name: Sunapha Yoga
findings.text: Planets other than the Sun occupy the 2nd house from the Moon. Indicates wealth acquired through one's own efforts, good intelligence, and a respectable status.

findings.name: Budhaditya Yoga
findings.text: Sun and Mercury are conjunct in the same sign. Confers intellectual agility, communicative ability, and scholarly interests. Very common as Mercury stays close to the Sun.

findings.name: Yogakaraka Planet
findings.text: A single planet rules both an angle (kendra) and a trine (trikona) for this ascendant, making it the most auspicious functional benefic in the chart. Its periods are generally productive.

findings.name: Raja Yoga (Kendra-Trikona Lords)
findings.text: The lord of an angle and the lord of a trine form an association through conjunction, mutual aspect, or sign exchange. Enhances status, authority, and prosperity, particularly in their dashas.

findings.name: Dhana Yoga
findings.text: Wealth lords (2nd or 11th) connect with dharma/lakshmi lords (1st, 5th, or 9th). Promotes accumulation of assets and financial prosperity, especially during their operating dashas.

findings.name: Parivartana Yoga (Mutual Reception)
findings.text: Two planets occupy each other's signs, intertwining the indications of their respective houses. The outcome depends on whether auspicious or challenging houses are involved.
